questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

She was amazed by / the unique architecture of / the Sydney Opera House.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. No error .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically correct and there are no errors in any of the parts.
 
• It is a simple declarative sentence that correctly uses the past tense ("was amazed") and the definite article ("the") before a proper noun ("Sydney Opera House").
 
• The structure of the sentence follows standard English syntax and conveys the intended meaning clearly.

Correct sentence: *She was amazed by the unique architecture of the Sydney Opera House.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The definite article "the" is used before a noun when the noun is specific and both the speaker and listener know what is being referred to.
 
• "Unique" is correctly used as an adjective describing the noun "architecture."

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He told / his senior, "I / will sung a song / at the party tonight."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. will sung a song .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is in the segment "will sung a song." The verb "sung" is the past participle form and is incorrectly used here.
 
• When using the simple future tense, the correct structure is "will" followed by the base form of the verb ("sing" in this case).

Correct sentence: *He told his senior, "I will sing a song at the party tonight."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple Future Tense Structure:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + will/shall + base verb.
 
• **Example:** She will call you tomorrow.
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions that will happen in the future.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

There was no one left in the world whom they could call ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**theirs**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The pronoun "**theirs**" is a possessive pronoun, meaning something that belongs to them.
 
• The sentence is talking about someone they could call as their own, thus the possessive pronoun "**theirs**" is correct.
 
• **Options 1, 2,** and **3** are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"There was no one left in the world whom they could call **theirs**__."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "there's"** is incorrect because it is a contraction of "there is".
 
• **Option 2: "their's"** is incorrect because there is no such grammatical contraction.
 
• **Option 3: "their"** is incorrect in this context; it is a possessive adjective and not a possessive pronoun.

questions.question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

The touch-sensitive surface is one of the reasons why tablets and smart phones are so smart. All touchscreens generate an electric field __________ the screen. Your finger interferes with the field, and the device's operating system __________ your touch or swipe.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**across; follows**'.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**across the screen**" is the appropriate choice as it implies the electric field being generated over the surface of the screen.
 
• The word "**follows**" fits well in the context as the operating system detects and responds to the user’s input.
 
• The other options: "**past; attends**," "**beyond; escorts**," and "**onto; chases**" do not fit the context or usual terminology associated with touchscreen technology.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The touch-sensitive surface is one of the reasons why tablets and smart phones are so smart. All touchscreens generate an electric field across__ the screen. Your finger interferes with the field, and the device's operating system __follows__ your touch or swipe.*

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Past**: implies moving by something or to a position further on in time.
 
• **Beyond**: suggests something that is further away or outside the range.
 
• **Onto**: implies movement to a position on a surface.
 
• **Attends**: means to be present at.
 
• **Escorts**: means to accompany someone or something somewhere.
 
• **Chases**: means to pursue with intent to catch up.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

options.text: It is a obvious that child needs love and attention of parents.
It is an obvious that child needs love and attention of parents.
It is obvious that a child needs love and attention of parents.
It is the obvious that child needs love and attention of parents.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. It is obvious that a child needs love and attention of parents. .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence should use the article "a" before the noun "child" because it refers to any child in general, not a specific one.
 
• The phrase "an obvious" is incorrect because "obvious" is an adjective and needs a noun. The correct phrase is "it is obvious" to describe a general statement.
 
• The phrase "of parents" should be preceded by "the" to specify the love and attention of parents in general.

Correct sentence: *It is obvious that a child needs love and attention of the parents.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article Usage: **

 
 
• **"A/An": **Used before singular nouns that are not specified.
 
• **"The": **Used before specific or previously mentioned nouns.
 
 
 
• **Adjective Placement:**
 
 
• Adjectives typically precede the nouns they modify and do not require an article when used in statements like "it is obvious."

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Maria was unhappy / because she terribly performed / in the examination / conducted last month.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. because she terribly performed .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment "because she terribly performed" contains the error.
 
• The adverb "terribly" should be positioned correctly to modify the verb "performed".
 
• The correct placement of the adverb should be after the verb in this context, i.e., "performed terribly".

Correct sentence: *Maria was unhappy because she performed terribly in the examination conducted last month.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adverb Placement: **

 
 
• Adverbs modifying verbs are typically placed immediately before or after the verb they modify depending on their emphasis.
 
• Example: "She sings beautifully" (the adverb "beautifully" modifies the verb "sings").
 
 
 
• **Correct Usage:**
 
 
• Example: "He quickly ran to the store" (the adverb "quickly" modifies the verb "ran").
 
• Incorrect: "He ran quick to the store." Correct: "He ran quickly to the store."
